items.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Ship to review, fix, and approve pull requests in beta
items.summary: Claude Ship handles PR review, CI fixes, merge conflicts, and approval decisions. Code Review is GA; PR Steward and Claude Approvals are in beta. Available on Claude Team and Enterprise plans for GitHub repos.
items.why: Claude Ship is the first AI tool handling the full PR cycle from review through fixes to approval. It could reshape how development teams manage code quality and release velocity.

items.headline: Gemini 4 agents discover faster quantum algorithms, all verified in the Lean theorem prover
items.summary: Teams of Gemini 4 agents found improvements to known quantum algorithms. Key results include an 11.8x cost reduction for a fusion-energy quantum circuit and a 290x speedup for arcsin. Google open-sourced the Lean library and verified solutions.

items.headline: OpenAI chief scientist proposes shared perplexity metric and development limits for frontier AI
items.summary: Jakub Pachocki argues cross-entropy loss should be a shared metric for comparing AI progress. OpenAI published internal figures: log-perplexity from 0.99 (GPT-3.5) to below 0.8 for current models. Proposes developers agree on common limits.

items.headline: Chat-tuned GPT-6.2 rolls out to ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users
items.summary: A version of GPT-6.2 optimized for the Chat tab is rolling out globally. OpenAI reports 71.7% image understanding (vs 47.4% for GPT-6) and 78.1% on difficult instructions (vs 62.5%). Safety adherence at 91-94%. Work and Codex models unchanged.

items.headline: OpenAI and Cisco launch Shirudo, an open-source eBPF runtime security tool for Linux
items.summary: Shirudo uses Linux eBPF to build shields that block exploit paths without restarts. Licensed BSD 2-Clause. A demo showed Codex generating a shield to block a Java4Shell exploit. December 15 webinar announced.

items.headline: Anthropic study finds AI mostly increases output rather than cutting jobs across 58 companies
items.summary: Based on 66 interviews at 58 U.S. companies (all Anthropic enterprise customers), the report finds AI mostly raises output rather than reducing headcount. About two-thirds of companies hired less. Nine cut contracted workers, mostly offshore.

items.headline: Anthropic deprecates Claude Opus 4.5, sets retirement for January 22, 2027
items.summary: Claude Opus 4.5 (claude-opus-4-5-20251101 and claude-opus-4-5) is deprecated and will be retired from the API on January 22, 2027. Anthropic recommends migrating to Opus 5.5.

items.headline: Claude launches Enterprise Frontier Safeguards beta with zero data retention
items.summary: Enterprise Frontier Safeguards provides zero data retention for eligible organizations. Encrypted safety data copies go to a customer-owned cloud bucket. Available on Claude Platform, AWS, and Google Cloud.

items.headline: SpaceXAI reportedly earns $3.1B per month renting compute to Anthropic, scales back own AI products
items.summary: The New York Times reports Anthropic is SpaceXAI's biggest compute customer at roughly $3.1B per month. SpaceXAI is reportedly scaling back some AI products including disbanding the Grok Imagine team and shutting down AI avatars.

items.headline: ChatGPT Dots always-on agents reportedly expanding to EU subscribers
items.summary: TestingCatalog reports that ChatGPT Dots, the always-on agent feature where each Dot has its own computer and works with connected apps, is rolling out to EU users.

items.headline: Google reportedly adds Gemini 4 Carbon to Antigravity for Pro subscribers with task checklists
items.summary: TestingCatalog and 9to5Google report Gemini 4 Carbon is now available to AI Pro users in Antigravity, previously Ultra-only. New features include live task checklists and orchestrator settings. Argon quota merging into the general bucket.
